qualifying_updates.title: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub announced public-preview local sandboxing for local repository and working-tree sessions in the Copilot app. Project settings cover additional read/write and read-only filesystem paths, denied folders, outbound and local network settings, and Git or GitHub CLI credential access. If the operating system cannot enforce the requested policy, the sandboxed shell fails instead of running without sandboxing.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is a concrete fail-closed execution policy for coding-agent shells, with separate filesystem, network, and credential scopes.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Governance pages should treat local agent sessions as execution environments with explicit filesystem, network, and credential policy, and should prefer fail-closed behavior when sandbox enforcement is unavailable.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route broad Copilot app feature coverage upstream; keep the local note focused on permission policy and fail-closed shell behavior.

qualifying_updates.title: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub added a dedicated personal code-review settings page across Copilot plans and an enterprise-level default review effort setting. Users can configure automatic review on pull-request creation, coauthoring, draft-to-ready transitions, new pushes, draft pull requests, and default Lite or Balanced review effort; enterprises can set inherited review-effort defaults with organization and repository overrides.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI review depth is becoming an explicit personal, repository, organization, and enterprise policy surface rather than an implicit model behavior.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Code-review operating guidance should record who owns default AI review effort, when automatic review is triggered, and where teams intentionally override enterprise defaults.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest should connect to existing review-configuration guidance without duplicating the GitHub product matrix.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub announced enterprise-managed OpenTelemetry configuration for Copilot app agent activity. Administrators can export traces of agent sessions, including model requests and tool use, to compatible monitoring tools; prompt and response content is excluded by default unless content-capture settings are reviewed and enabled.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice signal is centralized agent-session observability with privacy-sensitive content capture defaults.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent observability guidance should distinguish structural execution traces from captured prompt or response content, and should make content capture a reviewed governance decision.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Good evidence for local pages on traceability, audit logs, and privacy-preserving agent telemetry.

qualifying_updates.title: New features and improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains 1.18.0 added assisted approvals for low-risk tool calls, re-editing earlier messages with conversation and file-change rewind, organization and enterprise skills and custom instructions, Codex plan mode, built-in GitHub MCP Server toggles, and persistent per-tool MCP controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Several local practice surfaces converge here: risk-tiered approvals, rewindable conversation state, shared instruction packages, plan review before implementation, and persistent MCP tool governance.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Instruction and tool-governance pages should separate shared skills, organization-managed custom instructions, per-tool MCP controls, and human plan approval as distinct operating controls.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route product specifics upstream; retain the local pattern of approval tiers and persistent tool controls.

qualifying_updates.title: JetBrains Air: Building a System of Products for Agentic Software Development
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: JetBrains introduced JetBrains Air as a system spanning individual IDE agent work, team coordination, organizational governance, cost management, shared context, and multi-vendor agent support. The post frames agentic development as initiated, executed, coordinated, reviewed, and governed across surfaces, with Agent Client Protocol connecting IDEs to agent harnesses and observability.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is organizational: adoption pressure is moving beyond individual prompts toward shared context, policy, cost visibility, auditability, and accountability across multiple agents and vendors.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Operating-model pages should evaluate agent platforms by coordination, review, governance, cost, context, and accountability controls instead of treating model or agent choice as the whole adoption decision.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use only as downstream operating-model evidence; broad product and protocol entity coverage belongs upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Best MCP memory servers for teams using AI coding agents
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The post compares MCP memory options by team failure mode, distinguishing small local graphs, human-readable shared notes, hosted semantic recall, temporal graphs, and approved decision records. It proposes a two-agent test that checks whether a changed decision remains current, owned, and traceable across tools.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It gives local context architecture a practical test for whether memory is only storage/search or actually an authoritative team handoff and decision layer.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Memory guidance should require scope separation, stale-fact handling, human acceptance, owner/status metadata, and cross-agent retrieval tests before treating memory as team context.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest should avoid a catalog of MCP memory products and focus on the local memory-evaluation test.

qualifying_updates.title: CLAUDE.md vs agent memory: what each should store
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: The post separates stable project instructions, personal auto memory, temporary task handoffs, and shared team decisions. It recommends keeping commands, boundaries, conventions, and hard invariants in repository guidance while keeping secrets, ownerless exceptions, temporary plans, and mutable product or architecture decisions out of static instruction files.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local wiki already distinguishes durable instructions from task state; this source adds a current public framing for instruction hygiene and decision ownership.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Prompt and instruction pages should treat repository guidance as stable, scoped, reviewable behavior control, and route changing decisions to owner/status records instead of front-loading them into every agent session.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Good candidate for a downstream lens on instruction-file maintenance and task handoff boundaries.

qualifying_updates.title: Lumos Launches MCP Governance to Provide Agent Runtime Security
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Lumos announced MCP Governance for Claude Code and Codex, describing runtime permission checks that decide whether an AI agent action is allowed and block actions when policy denies them.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Although the vendor and product are upstream-owned, the practice signal is local: governed tool access is shifting toward point-of-action permission decisions in agent runtimes.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: MCP governance guidance should distinguish server registration, tool inventory, approval prompts, and runtime policy enforcement at the moment an agent acts.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep only the governed-MCP practice lens downstream; route product background upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Cut AI agent cost and improve accuracy with Code Execution in the Datadog MCP Server
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Datadog described generally available Code Execution for its MCP Server. Agents use execute_code and search_datadog_sdk to run sandboxed JavaScript, query several Datadog APIs, keep intermediate data in code, filter large responses before returning them to the model, and rely on the trusted MCP service to apply caller permissions while keeping credentials outside the sandbox.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice pattern is a bounded execution substrate for multi-step tool work: deterministic joining, filtering, parallel querying, and intermediate state can move out of model context while preserving permission checks.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Tool-call practice should compare conversation-level tool chaining with sandboxed generated-code execution, especially for token cost, evidence minimization, credential isolation, and permission boundaries.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Focus any ingest on MCP code-execution boundaries rather than a Datadog product page.

qualifying_updates.title: Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: GitHub described rebuilding a pull-request diff surface for a million-line PR with hundreds of inline comments. The post emphasizes bounded lazy measurement, scroll anchoring, structure-first streaming, off-main-thread highlighting, production instrumentation, objective health signals, a mock-server headless probe lane, and an unattended desktop-app autopilot loop.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent-generated migrations and broad refactors can create review surfaces that fail under large diffs and many comments; the practice signal is to define measurable review-surface invariants and automate reproduction rather than relying on visual inspection.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Review-workflow and application-pattern pages should treat diff review as an inspectable system with performance budgets, runtime probes, and unattended repro loops when AI-assisted changes increase PR scale.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential local follow-up: large-PR review ergonomics and instrumentation for AI-generated migration branches.

qualifying_updates.title: Qodo's 2026 State of AI Code Quality Report Reveals Growing Verification Challenge as Agentic Development Scales
qualifying_updates.short_factual_summary: Qodo announced a 2026 AI code quality report based on research conducted August 7-14, 2026 with 500 U.S. software developers and 300 U.S. engineering leaders at organizations using AI meaningfully in the SDLC. The release frames agentic-development scale as creating a verification challenge and describes full-repository signals, prior PR decisions, explainable feedback, reduced noise, and organization-specific standards as quality controls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local practice signal is adoption-stage pressure: code generation velocity needs matching verification, repository context, prior-decision evidence, and organization-specific standards.
named_entities: 2026 State of AI Code Quality Report
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Verification pages should connect agentic scale to explainable review evidence, repository-wide context, historical PR decisions, and organization-specific quality standards.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Treat as vendor-sponsored survey evidence; verify details against the full report before turning any statistics into durable wiki claims.
